pod.raw: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC
pod.statement: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC.
pod.baselineContext: In the attested record of 48 BC, Mediterranean stood at a hinge: what was written and copied there set the ceiling on what later centuries could know. Nearby in the record: Fire reaches the Library of Alexandria (48 BC). The divergence departs from that settled course.

eras.title: Two Years of Aftermath
eras.summary: Two years of consequences arrive in the order consequences always do: first prices, then postures, then paperwork. The great structures hold; their assumptions do not.
eras.detail:
Two years of consequences arrive in the order consequences always do: first prices, then postures, then paperwork. The great structures hold; their assumptions do not. The span from -48 to -46 reads, in retrospect, as one argument conducted in many registers: what would the ordinary strains of a changed world be allowed to cost, and who would pay it.

The record answers through its events. The archive stands (48 BC); The Mouseion of Alexandria convenes over the changed course (48 BC); Grain prices shift in the Alexandria markets (47 BC). Each was a partial discharge of the same accumulated pressure, none a settlement. The registers record it drily; the letters that survive do not.

By -46 the question had not been answered so much as re-priced. What the era settled, it settled in habits and ledgers rather than treaties; what it left loaded, the next era would inherit with interest.

eras.summary: Between -46 and -38, the divergence stops being news and starts being structure: technique spillover sets the agenda, and the Ptolemaic Egypt adjusts.

events.title: The archive stands
events.summary: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC. In Alexandria the criers say little and the letter-writers say too much; between them, a usable account of the new situation takes a season to form.

deltas.note: The immediate shock is absorbed; the accounting begins.

plausibility.rationale: Direct restatement of the divergence itself; the least contingent claim in the timeline.

events.title: The Mouseion of Alexandria convenes over the changed course
events.summary: The Mouseion of Alexandria meets in extraordinary session. Sosigenes of Alexandria argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

deltas.note: The institution claims the divergence as its business.
Responsibility, and visibility, attach to the one who asked for the record.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions reliably respond to discontinuity with procedure; the specific convenor is the contingent part.

events.title: Grain prices shift in the Alexandria markets
events.summary: The first measurable consequence arrives where it always does: in prices. Grain moves against last season's rate in Alexandria, and porters, brokers, and household stewards adjust before any council does.

deltas.note: The exchequer notices what the market already knew.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable early transmission channel of any structural change.

events.title: The Roman Republic recalculates
events.summary: In the chanceries of the Roman Republic, the first response is to ask for better copies of the dispatches. The second is to move money. Only the third, months later, is anything resembling a policy.

deltas.note: The rival’s settled policy quietly goes back to committee.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors always reprice risk after a discontinuity; the two-year lag matches the speed of credible intelligence.

events.title: The markets reprice around Ptolemaic Egypt
events.summary: A working method has left the workshops that guarded it; The Roman Republic can no longer control who learns it. Brokers adjust before any edict: contracts shorten, surety costs rise, and household stewards change what they store.

deltas.note: The market hedges; kitchens follow.

plausibility.rationale: Price adjustment is the most reliable transmission channel of structural pressure.

events.title: A working technique crosses the Roman Republic's border
events.summary: What the Mouseion of Alexandria kept close now travels with journeymen. A dispute of principle inside The Roman Republic is becoming a dispute of office.

deltas.note: Knowledge proves cheaper to hire than to guard.
A new name starts appearing in the registers.

plausibility.rationale: Techniques diffuse along wage gradients; guarding them raises the wage.

events.title: The Mouseion of Alexandria revises what the young are taught
events.summary: Over the following season the old arrangement gives way. A new syllabus fixes the changed world into schoolroom fact. Two lean years in the districts around The Roman Republic would exhaust the granary math. Children now learn as ordinary what their grandparents called impossible.

deltas.note: The syllabus quietly rewrites what counts as common knowledge.

plausibility.rationale: Institutions metabolize discontinuity into curriculum within a generation. Revised after review: the mechanism is now named instead of asserted.

events.summary: Too much of what The Roman Republic eats and sells moves along a single corridor that others can tax or close. A probe at the margin (an envoy recalled, a toll raised, a garrison reinforced) measures how much the world has actually changed.

deltas.note: The rival prices the new equilibrium in small provocations.

plausibility.rationale: Neighbors test any settlement whose guarantors look distracted.

body.subhead: From our own correspondents; the particulars as far as they can be known

paragraphs: The Library of Alexandria never burns in 48 BC. In Alexandria the criers say little and the letter-writers say too much; between them, a usable account of the new situation takes a season to form.

Those closest to the affair counsel patience; those furthest from it, as usual, counsel everything else. The Mouseion of Alexandria is said to be preparing an accounting, which is what it is always said to be preparing.

columns.heading: The view from the grain exchange
paragraphs: Prices answered before opinions did. Dealers in grain report the season's contracts rewritten twice in a fortnight, and the porters, who always know first, have raised their rates.
It is meanwhile reported that position=well-placed observer; reputation=rising.

notices: Grain measures certified at the temple scales; short measures answer to the eparch.
A copyist, neat hand, seeks engagement by the season. Ask at the second colonnade.
Lost: one seal-ring, lion device. Reward in silver, no questions.

artifacts.title: Letter of Theodotos of Chios on the mouseion of alexandria convenes over the changed course

paragraphs: You will have heard some version of it by now, so let me give you the true one before rumor improves it further. The Mouseion of Alexandria meets in extraordinary session. Sosigenes of Alexandria argues that the moment must be committed to record before rumor rewrites it; a survey of holdings, obligations, and precedents is ordered.

What it means for us: the grain contracts must be re-sworn, and I would not extend credit past the season until we see how the Mouseion of Alexandria settles. Aunt Zoe asks after your health and whether the northern road is safe; I have told her yes to the first and lied about the second.
Send word by the first reliable carrier. And send the account-book. The real one.
body.postscript: P.S. The price of candles has doubled. Draw your own conclusions about how late the council is sitting.

interpretations.gloss: Read the accounts and "Sosigenes of Alexandria sets the fashion of the season" stops being a decision at all. The money had already moved; what the chronicles record as a choice is the moment somebody finally wrote down an arrangement that had been operating for two seasons. Our rivals want a villain here. We have a ledger, and the ledger balances.

"Sosigenes of Alexandria sets the fashion of the season" happened because three people in one room preferred it to the alternative in front of them, and the alternative in front of them was not the one posterity imagines. The Ledger School will tell you the money decided. The money was available for either course. Somebody chose.

The registers show the change arriving in the district a full generation before "Sosigenes of Alexandria sets the fashion of the season" is supposed to have caused it: fewer apprentices bound, more women in the trades, the old feast quietly dropped. What the assembly did that year was ratify a fact. The event is a date the capital gave to something the country had already finished doing.
